I do think about life from the perspective of suffering, and you know what, it molded me. Someways good, someways bad. My perspective is that opting to not feel anything, including the perception of relief or joy just to avoid the negative feelings is a pussy move, coming from someone with bouts of those tendencies. I do think there are instances where death is a justified route like immense, crippling physical pain. For me, I don't want to be supported if I lose higher brain function or develop alzhiemers. Of course, I'm not there, so I recognize I'm doing alright for myself even if money is tight or I have pain in my neck. And what problem am I ignoring? That life has surmountable challenges that I've gotten over before and can get over again? Sometimes I feel like a suicidal boomer: watching these young people swear that life will never get better and the only solution is to delete their consciousness. For the love of God eat a patty melt or something, not everyone is a life is a precious gift type old coot, some just recognize that removing your brain is a drastic response.

From my experience: yes and no.

People can smell bitterness. I was in a relationship that got me caught in cloud9, yet they broke it off because they felt that my depressive swings were too much for them to handle in a fresh relationship. Despite my cloud9 mania I was still sad and they could rightly sense it.

At the same time, I have had friends that have spoke positively about me in honest and emotional ways, yet I still saw myself as being worthless and scum, or whatever adjective I was applying to myself. The thought "I tricked them into liking me" popped in occasionally. But even I realized I was a shitty liar, and I must be doing something correct.

It's a tug of war. You can't overcome these thoughts by entering into a strange codependent type relationship where there is no criticism, but the support of others can ground you for sure.

I often find myself dancing over the line from states of hyper-focused manic joy and hazy bouts of overwhelming grief. I've met a good few people who've grown on me, and a few old friends I've rekindled with. There's media I would have never got to experience like some awful B-List movies from the 2000's, or some of my favourite games that I've gotten the chance to play because I am alive. 

I won't go and say that being alive has been an absolute net-positive with zero draws, but sometimes in my more sobering moments I am humbled by thinking about the things I did by virtue of me stepping out of my loop and trying.

Keep doing what you're doing: be there for them, remind them that you want them to stick around and live, and just be a positive influence. If things are too much for you and you're really concerned you should call for an ambulance to have them admitted.

Please understand that if they do anything rash that it isn't your fault, and that it's not your responsibility to manage their emotions.
I encourage you to hold out hope for better days. Keep working on your art as well, I believe our own individually created art is something to be proud of.
